him wiping off the oil hurt me. im a blade smith mainly but i do a bit of blacksmithing. (for those who dont understand the difference. blade smiths are the black smiths that smith swords and other kinds of blades. blacksmiths smith a variety of other things including knives and metal work. but metal work is more of a metal worker's specialty. but anyways blade smiths tend to oil a blade before giving it to the customer to help prevent rust. also for those who are confused on how a handle on a sword is attached. when the sword is made the tang is attatched. it then has 2-3 holes drilled/punched through as the handle/hilt is then made or bought and then fit to the tang. im still new to blade smithing. also oil quenching is different from water quenching. yes water quenching is good and works but it can cause the metal to fracture and crack faster as it vents all the heat upwards due to super heating. oil quenching is more preferred as it cools it evenly. due to how flammable oil is it retains heat allowing the blade to quench and start the hardening process without to many fractures. if they blade was made to thin or to weak from a non-carbonated metal it can fracture. but the carbon state of metal is something to speak of in another comment.) also it was A bladesmith who make katana'S (most of the terminology i said doesn't fully apply to katana's)
